header: "Which departments did this answer actually cover?" -- the SYSTEM computes this from the SQL; the model does not write it. The model's plain-English reading can drift from what its SQL does (it once described one department while the SQL matched a pattern that covered seven). So for every answer that filters by department through a sub-query on nlq.departments, I run the same sub-query on its own and show the matched department names next to the answer. The line appears for an answer that FILTERS by department, however the model worded that filter (a sub-query on nlq.departments, a JOIN with d.code IN (...), department_id / department_code / department conditions). An answer with no department filter shows no line, and neither does an EXCLUSION ("not in C&IT"). I list only departments that really hold people in the answer. A department filter such as "C&IT (all its sections)" matches three department records, but executives usually sit under ONE of them and the granular sections hold the non-executives. So I narrow the filter's matches to the departments where at least one person satisfying the answer's OWN conditions (cohort, designation, ...) works: an executive answer names only departments that have executives, a non-executive answer only those that have non-executives. Deliberately conservative: I report only a scope I can compute exactly. A sub-query that cannot run on its own (e.g. it refers to a column of the outer query), and sub-queries under NOT / NOT IN (which EXCLUDE departments), never produce a scope; the answer is then shown without one.

symbols.name: departmentScopeQueries
doc: Builds a standalone `SELECT code, name FROM nlq.departments WHERE ...` for each department sub-query.

symbols.name: peopleFootprintQuery
symbols.sig: export function peopleFootprintQuery(sql: string): string | null
doc: Builds a standalone query: which departments hold at least one person who satisfies the answer's own WHERE (cohort, designation, department filter ...), grouped by department record. JOINs are fine (the model often joins nlq.departments just to read a department code): I keep the FROM and WHERE as written and only the person table (nlq.employees, under whatever alias the answer gave it) supplies the department. Returns null when the answer's shape does not allow that to be computed exactly (no person table or two of them, a sub-select in FROM, a set operation, a CTE, HAVING ...). I drop ORDER BY / LIMIT / GROUP BY of the original: the question is "where do these people work", not "which ten".

symbols.name: NEGATING_BINARY
symbols.sig: const NEGATING_BINARY = new Set(["NOT IN", "NOT LIKE", "NOT ILIKE", "!=", "<>"])

symbols.name: departmentFilterInfo
symbols.sig: export function departmentFilterInfo(sql: string): { has: boolean; negated: boolean } | null
doc: I check whether the answer's SQL filters by department (in WHERE, or in a JOIN condition), and whether any such condition is an exclusion. A department column compared with another column (the plain join condition e.department_id = d.id) is NOT a filter. Returns null when the SQL cannot be read.

symbols.name: computeDepartmentScope
symbols.sig: export async function computeDepartmentScope(client: SqlClient, sql: string): Promise<DepartmentScope | null>
doc: Returns the departments that hold the people in this answer, for an answer that filters by department; null when the answer has no department filter, excludes departments, or has a shape whose people cannot be located exactly.
